answer: Random Selection Ledger (RSL) assigns identity verification slots through verifiable randomness sourced from an external beacon that cannot be precomputed. Each candidate must solve a unique one-time computation puzzle derived from the random seed, making the ledge of required work infeasible to front-run. Without access to the future random value, an attacker cannot prepare sufficient identities in advance, turning the fable of cheap Sybil resistance into a costly reality where each river of attempted forgeries meets deterministic computational barriers.
